physicalNotes: Radius: WASP-189 is a rapid rotator. Deline et al. (2022), A&A 659, A74 fit the CHEOPS transits of WASP-189 b with a gravity-darkened oblate star: equatorial radius 2.363 solar radii and a polar radius 2.88% smaller (Table 3), so a polar radius of 2.2949. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, (2.363^2 x 2.2949)^(1/3) = 2.3401 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202142400); the scene draws the flattening, with the equatorial radius on the outline. Mass 2.03 +/- 0.066 solar masses from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 8000 +/- 80 K from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis, the spin axis measured against WASP-189 b's orbit, is up.
